note: Generated file — do not edit. Regenerate with `tools/lab format sync`; `tools/lab validate` fails if it has drifted from the code.

campaign.note: population.json is the live state of a campaign, written only by `lab run`: one entry per candidate plus the campaign's status, best candidate, budgets spent, usage-governor state, final score and claim.
campaign.claim_note: Written once by `lab run` from the final split against the success_threshold fixed in campaign.toml before the run. `untested` while the search runs.

candidates.fitness_note: `fitness` is the search-split score, read by `lab eval` only; higher or lower is better per campaign.toml [report].higher_is_better. It is optimistic by construction; the final score in population.json `final` is one read of the untouched final split.

feed_classes.news: homepage news column; eligible for RSS
feed_classes.activity: project activity timeline only; never RSS
feed_classes.none: chart data; never a feed item

provenance.note: Which model produced a candidate — two facts, kept apart: `requested` is the worker model named in campaign.toml, `served` is what actually answered, read from the session result the worker stores (session.json, modelUsage).

sources.session.json modelUsage: served: the models that answered the session
sources.none: no session ran (the baseline) or no result was stored

provenance.cost_note: session.json total_cost_usd is the list-price equivalent `claude -p` reports; on a subscription it is a measure of usage, not a bill.

ledger.note: One row per candidate, written only by `lab run`; never deleted.
